translation: Arjuna said: Between those devotees who are permanently integrated and worship You through active service, and those who contemplate the unmanifest, imperishable Absolute (Aksharam Avyaktam), who possesses a more perfect grasp of the science of Yoga?

The Blessed Lord said: Those who focus their minds single-mindedly upon My presence, and serve Me day and night with intense devotion and unswerving faith—they are evaluated by Me as the most perfectly integrated in Yoga (yuktatamah).
But those who contemplate the indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, inconceivable, changeless, unmoving, and eternal Imperishable Absolute;

By thoroughly subduing the entire network of their senses, maintaining an equal, impartial intellect under all circumstances (sarvatra sama-buddhayah), and dedicating their lives actively to the welfare of all living creatures (sarva-bhuta-hite ratah)—they also arrive at Me alone.
simple_explanation: Note the mandatory ethical clause: one cannot attain the unmanifest Absolute by sitting in an ivory tower while ignoring the suffering of the world. Active engagement in the welfare of all creatures (sarva-bhuta-hita) is a structural requirement for both paths.

translation: The psychological friction and difficulty (kleshah) encountered by those whose minds are attached to the unmanifest Absolute is far greater. For a clear realization of an unmanifest destination is exceptionally grueling to secure for human beings who remain anchored in physical body-consciousness.
But those who surrender all their daily actions unto My cosmic law, look upon Me as their supreme goal, and meditate upon Me with unswerving, single-minded focus;

To them whose hearts are completely integrated within My awareness, O Partha, I swiftly manifest as the absolute Deliverer who lifts them straight out of the crashing ocean of this death-bound world (mrityu-samsara-sagarat).

Settle your thoughts securely within My universal presence, and anchor your analytical intellect within My divine law. Doing so, you will reside permanently within Me hereafter; there is absolutely no doubt about this.
If you are unable to fix your mind steadily upon Me without wavering, O Dhananjaya, then strive to reach Me by the systematic practice of repetitive concentration (Abhyasa-yogena).

If you lack the focus to practice repetitive exercises, then shift your focus entirely to My active work (mat-karma-paramoh bhava). Even by executing daily, structural actions for the sake of My global mission, you will achieve perfection.

And if you find yourself unable to execute even this mission work, then take refuge in My path, discipline your lower self, and systematically practice the complete renunciation of the personal fruits of all your labor (sarva-karma-phala-tyagam).
simple_explanation: Look at the scientific fallback options Krishna provides. If you cannot manage abstract meditation, practice corporate mission work. If you cannot manage corporate work, simply do your daily accounting or plumbing jobs honestly, throwing away the mental anxiety for personal prizes. Detachment can be unlocked at any point in human labor.

translation: Cultivating intellectual knowledge (Jnana) is superior to the mechanical repetition of practices without understanding. Deep meditation (Dhyana) is superior to bookish knowledge. And the active renunciation of the fruits of action (karma-phala-tyagah) is superior to meditation; for immediately following upon such renunciation, absolute inner peace (Shanti) is unlocked.

He who harbors absolutely no hatred or malice toward any living creature, who is naturally friendly and compassionate to all, free from the illusion of ownership (nirmamah), free from egoism (nirahankarah), completely balanced in both pleasure and pain, and patiently forgiving;

Constantly content, well-integrated in Yoga, self-controlled, possessed of iron-clad resolve (dridha-nishchayah), with his mind and intellect completely dedicated to Me—that devotee is exceedingly dear to Me.

He by whose presence the world is never agitated or broken into panic, and who is himself never thrown into anxiety by the actions of the world, who is entirely liberated from the grip of personal exultation, envy, fear, and mental fever—he is dear to Me.

He who is free from personal expectations, pure in body and mind, highly efficient and skilled in his work (dakshah), detached from personal outcomes, free from mental trauma or distress, and has completely cast off the lower instinct for reward-driven undertakings—that devotee is dear to Me.

He who neither exults in transient gain nor hates unexpected loss, who neither grieves over past failures nor craves future prizes, and who has systematically risen above the calculations of personal good and bad fortunes—that devotional practitioner is dear to Me.

He who remains completely equal and unbiased toward an adversary or a companion, unswerving under public honor or stinging disgrace, balanced amidst cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and entirely free from limiting attachments;

To whom public slander and lavish praise hold equal weight, who maintains internal control over his speech, content with whatever basic resources come his way, free from hoarding or obsessive attachment to a physical home (aniketah), and possessed of a rock-solid, stable intellect—that human being is deeply dear to Me.

But those who absorb and actively practice this life-giving, nectar of righteous wisdom (dharmyamritam) exactly as I have just detailed it, endowed with unshakeable faith and looking upon Me as their absolute goal—those devotees are exceedingly, immeasurably dear to Me.
